source: Thesis table 6.1 — joint display integrating the survey (N = 446) and the interviews (N = 10)
note: In a convergent design the two strands are analysed separately and compared at the end. The display is where they meet — including where they disagree.

rows.quantitative: C4 rents 4.39, 88.1% agree — the highest-scoring item in the survey, and uniform across districts (p = 0.193)
rows.convergenceNote: Convergence plus mechanism: the interviews explain how it happens

rows.quantitative: C1 graded: Kazimierz 3.77 / Old Town 3.31 / Podgórze 2.47 (ε² = 0.177)
rows.qualitative: T2 — a night that isn't ours
T3 — the infrastructure of everyday life
T4 — from home to stage set
rows.convergenceNote: Convergence plus depth: the metaphors name what the scale measures
The survey shows how much; the interviews show who, and why

rows.quantitative: F1 trust 1.99–2.24, uniformly low (p = 0.189); only 8.5% agree the city manages tourism effectively
rows.qualitative: T6 — 9 of 10 call for STR regulation, unprompted

rows.quantitative: G1 13.9–17.8%, not significant between districts; logit: costs OR 5.54, tenure OR 1.45, ownership OR 0.44
rows.qualitative: T8 — a continuum from decided to anchored; the anchored are owner-pensioners and long-rooted families
rows.convergenceNote: The one divergence: longer tenure weakly raises intention to leave in the model, while the most rooted interviewees say they are staying. Ownership, not tenure, carries the protective effect

rows.quantitative: Typology k = 2: In conflict 57.3% / Reconciled 42.7%; demographics not significant
rows.qualitative: Interview portraits map onto both types
rows.convergenceNote: Attitudes are polarised rather than uniform — an argument against reading Doxey's Irridex as a single linear stage
